bull_bear.body:
- Comprehensive in-house manufacturing capability spanning hot and cold forging presses and open-die hammers, supported by in-house tool rooms
- Long-term strategic partnerships with customers, with collaborative work on mitigating rising input costs for mutual long-term benefit
- Focus on high value engineered forgings, precision forging and machined components as a differentiated niche
- Stable and harmonious industrial relations with a workforce of 221 personnel supported by structured training and HR initiatives
- Access to shared infrastructure and services within the L.G. Balakrishnan & Bros group ecosystem (power, spares, processing, conversion and service arrangements disclosed in the related-party note)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Input cost inflation and raw material availability — Management names fluctuations in input costs along with availability as a key risk area. The ongoing West Asia energy crisis is described as disrupting raw material availability, leading to rising input prices and processing costs that pose significant challenges in the short to mid term and will affect manufacturing efficiency and on-time delivery of products. Steel forging is raw-material intensive, so the Company is dependent on passing these costs to customers, which it says it is negotiating for mutual long-term benefit.
- Recruitment and retention of workforce — Explicitly listed by management as a key risk area. The Company employs 221 personnel, so the loss of skilled forging and machining operators is material relative to its size; it mitigates through structured training programmes and HR initiatives.
- Cyber security threats — Named by management as one of three key risk areas in the MD&A Risks and Concerns section, addressed through strategies and control measures under the risk management framework.
- Single-segment and single end-industry concentration — The Company operates in only one segment, viz., Forging and Machining, and the automotive sector remains at the forefront of its end markets. There is no segmental diversification to buffer a downturn in automotive demand.
- Energy cost exposure and dependence on conventional power — Rising energy costs are cited as pressuring global manufacturing and supply chains including the forging industry, and higher energy prices were cited in the IMF's downward revision of India's FY2026-27 growth forecast. Forging is energy intensive; the Company is mitigating via solar power at one plant and a renewable-energy procurement agreement entered into during June 2026 (sourced from the Directors' Report Annexure B in the same annual report).
- Geopolitical tension and global macro uncertainty affecting demand and supply chains — Management notes that recent geopolitical tensions, evolving trade patterns and intermittent volatility in energy and commodity prices continue to pressure global manufacturing and supply chains, and that businesses across industries remained cautious in making fresh investments amid economic uncertainty.
- Regulatory and statutory cost changes — The New Labour Codes implication resulted in an estimated one-time increase in the provision for employee benefits during the year under review, illustrating the Company's exposure to changes in labour and statutory requirements.
- Execution risk on the new Chennai facility — The Chennai facility is stated to be poised to start operations by the end of the second quarter of 2026 and is relied upon to keep up with customer demands; delay or a slow ramp would leave customer demand unserved (sourced from the MD&A Business Environment Outlook and Prospects section of the same annual report).

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the manufacturing footprint through continuous focus on operational drivers, long-term strategic partnerships with customers and a special focus on high value engineered forgings
- Strengthen core manufacturing teams in planning, executing and managing efficient operational systems specifically aligned with customer requirements, without hampering production and delivery
- Commission the Chennai facility, expected to start operations by the end of the second quarter of 2026, to keep up with customer demand
- Sustain focus on asset management, maintenance and technological upgradation to improve operational efficiency and meet customer demands
- Work closely with customers to mitigate rising input costs on a mutually beneficial long-term basis, alongside process and resource optimisation measures
- Serve both automotive and industrial segments from a single Forging and Machining segment, using in-house hot and cold forging presses, open-die hammers and tool rooms
- Reduce dependence on conventional power by using solar at one plant and by contracting renewable energy supply from June 2026 for a portion of electricity requirements (sourced from the Directors' Report Annexure B energy-conservation disclosure)
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company is continuing to strengthen its manufacturing footprint with continuous focus on operational drivers, long-term strategic partnerships with customers and a special focus on high value engineered forgings. The principal expansion item disclosed is a new Chennai facility, which management states is poised to start operations by the end of the second quarter of 2026 and which is expected to help the Company keep up with customer demands. Sustained focus on asset management, maintenance and technological upgradation is described as key to improving operational efficiency. On the energy side, the Company already uses solar power at one of its plants and, during June 2026, entered into an agreement with a solar power supplier for the procurement of renewable energy to meet a portion of its electricity requirements (this and the Chennai commissioning language are sourced across the MD&A and the Directors' Report Annexure B in the same annual report). The Company reports no material changes, events or commitments affecting its financial position between the end of the financial year and the date of the report, and states that expenditure incurred on Research and Development was Nil.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The forging industry is expected to grow steadily, driven by recovering automotive demand, expanding industrial applications and ongoing capital investments
- India's strong manufacturing capabilities and supply chain diversification position it as an attractive global sourcing hub
- Long-term opportunities for the forging industry are well positioned across various industry sectors, though the automotive sector remains at the forefront
- Government support through various initiatives and a strong push on infrastructure investments are demand drivers for various forging components
- Emerging markets for high value forging such as precision forging or machined components across all sectors indicate long-term opportunities and growth
- Revenue growth of 10% was achieved despite rising input costs and volatile forecasts, mainly due to measures taken to improve process and resource optimisation
- The ongoing West Asia energy crisis is disrupting raw material availability, raising input prices and processing costs, which will affect manufacturing efficiency and on-time delivery in the short to mid term
- Recent geopolitical tensions, rising energy costs and persistent inflation continue to pressure global manufacturing and supply chains, including the forging industry
- India's medium-term growth outlook remains positive, anchored by a large domestic market and favourable demographic profile, despite the IMF revising the FY2026-27 forecast down to 6.4% from 6.5% in July 2026

- Commission the Chennai facility, expected to start operations by the end of the second quarter of 2026, to keep up with customer demand
- Sustain focus on asset management, maintenance and technological upgradation to improve operational efficiency and meet customer demands
- Work closely with customers to mitigate rising input costs on a mutually beneficial long-term basis, alongside process and resource optimisation measures
- Serve both automotive and industrial segments from a single Forging and Machining segment, using in-house hot and cold forging presses, open-die hammers and tool rooms

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company is continuing to strengthen its manufacturing footprint with continuous focus on operational drivers, long-term strategic partnerships with customers and a special focus on high value engineered forgings. The principal expansion item disclosed is a new Chennai facility, which management states is poised to start operations by the end of the second quarter of 2026 and which is expected to help the Company keep up with customer demands. Sustained focus on asset management, maintenance and technological upgradation is described as key to improving operational efficiency. On the energy side, the Company already uses solar power at one of its plants and, during June 2026, entered into an agreement with a solar power supplier for the procurement of renewable energy to meet a portion of its electricity requirements (this and the Chennai commissioning language are sourced across the MD&A and the Directors' Report Annexure B in the same annual report). The Company reports no material changes, events or commitments affecting its financial position between the end of the financial year and the date of the report, and states that expenditure incurred on Research and Development was Nil.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Comprehensive in-house manufacturing capability spanning hot and cold forging presses and open-die hammers, supported by in-house tool rooms
- Long-term strategic partnerships with customers, with collaborative work on mitigating rising input costs for mutual long-term benefit
- Focus on high value engineered forgings, precision forging and machined components as a differentiated niche
- Stable and harmonious industrial relations with a workforce of 221 personnel supported by structured training and HR initiatives
- Access to shared infrastructure and services within the L.G. Balakrishnan & Bros group ecosystem (power, spares, processing, conversion and service arrangements disclosed in the related-party note)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Input cost inflation and raw material availability — Management names fluctuations in input costs along with availability as a key risk area. The ongoing West Asia energy crisis is described as disrupting raw material availability, leading to rising input prices and processing costs that pose significant challenges in the short to mid term and will affect manufacturing efficiency and on-time delivery of products. Steel forging is raw-material intensive, so the Company is dependent on passing these costs to customers, which it says it is negotiating for mutual long-term benefit.
- Recruitment and retention of workforce — Explicitly listed by management as a key risk area. The Company employs 221 personnel, so the loss of skilled forging and machining operators is material relative to its size; it mitigates through structured training programmes and HR initiatives.
- Cyber security threats — Named by management as one of three key risk areas in the MD&A Risks and Concerns section, addressed through strategies and control measures under the risk management framework.
- Single-segment and single end-industry concentration — The Company operates in only one segment, viz., Forging and Machining, and the automotive sector remains at the forefront of its end markets. There is no segmental diversification to buffer a downturn in automotive demand.
- Energy cost exposure and dependence on conventional power — Rising energy costs are cited as pressuring global manufacturing and supply chains including the forging industry, and higher energy prices were cited in the IMF's downward revision of India's FY2026-27 growth forecast. Forging is energy intensive; the Company is mitigating via solar power at one plant and a renewable-energy procurement agreement entered into during June 2026 (sourced from the Directors' Report Annexure B in the same annual report).
- Geopolitical tension and global macro uncertainty affecting demand and supply chains — Management notes that recent geopolitical tensions, evolving trade patterns and intermittent volatility in energy and commodity prices continue to pressure global manufacturing and supply chains, and that businesses across industries remained cautious in making fresh investments amid economic uncertainty.
- Regulatory and statutory cost changes — The New Labour Codes implication resulted in an estimated one-time increase in the provision for employee benefits during the year under review, illustrating the Company's exposure to changes in labour and statutory requirements.
- Execution risk on the new Chennai facility — The Chennai facility is stated to be poised to start operations by the end of the second quarter of 2026 and is relied upon to keep up with customer demands; delay or a slow ramp would leave customer demand unserved (sourced from the MD&A Business Environment Outlook and Prospects section of the same annual report).
